text_blocks.snippet: Early signs of type 2 diabetes include increased thirst, frequent urination, and constant fatigue as high blood sugar builds up in the body.
snippet_highlighted_words: increased thirst, frequent urination, and constant fatigue

list.snippet: Frequent urination: Your kidneys work overtime to clear extra sugar, causing you to pee more often, especially at night.
Increased thirst: Fluid loss from frequent urination leads to constant thirst and dry mouth.
Persistent fatigue: Without enough insulin, glucose cannot enter your cells for energy, leaving you exhausted.
Blurred vision: High blood sugar changes fluid levels and swells the lenses in your eyes.
Slow-healing sores: Elevated glucose impairs blood flow and your immune system, making cuts heal slowly.
Tingling or numbness: Peripheral nerve damage can cause a prickling feeling or loss of sensation in your hands and feet.
Darkened skin patches: Velvety dark areas in body folds like the neck or armpits (acanthosis nigricans) signal insulin resistance.

text_blocks.snippet: You can read more about indicators and risk factors on the Mayo Clinic or review details on WebMD.
